\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دلیر} (diler)}{دلیر (diler)}]{\ur{دلیر} (diler) — bold}

\label{lesson:UR-C460-diler}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for miserly, then the Urdu for alms.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دلیر}}
\textbf{\ur{دلیر}} — \emph{diler} — \textquotedblleft{}bold\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{دلیر} \ur{لڑکی} \ur{اکیلی} \ur{پہاڑ} \ur{پر} \ur{چڑھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh diler laṛkī akelī pahāṛ par chaṛhī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That bold girl climbed the mountain alone.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دلیر}} (\emph{diler}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{dilēr}, \textquotedblleft{}bold\textquotedblright{}, a word built on \emph{dil}, \textquotedblleft{}heart\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ur{دل}}).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{diler}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{diler}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh diler laṛkī akelī pahāṛ par chaṛhī.} — That bold girl climbed the mountain alone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for miserly, then the Urdu for alms, then say \emph{diler} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{دلیر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Bold\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جانباز} (jānbāz)}{جانباز (jānbāz)}]{\ur{جانباز} (jānbāz) — daring; ready to risk one's life}

\label{lesson:UR-C460-janbaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for alms, then the Urdu for bold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جانباز}}
\textbf{\ur{جانباز}} — \emph{jānbāz} — \textquotedblleft{}daring; ready to risk one's life\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جانباز} \ur{سپاہی} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{بچایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jānbāz sipāhī ne bachche ko bachāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The daring soldier saved the child.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جانباز}} (\emph{jānbāz}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{jānbāz}, \textquotedblleft{}one who stakes his life\textquotedblright{}: \emph{jān}, \textquotedblleft{}life\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{bāz}, \textquotedblleft{}playing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جوکھم} (jokham)}{جوکھم (jokham)}]{\ur{جوکھم} (jokham) — a risk}

\label{lesson:UR-C460-jokham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for bold, then the Urdu for daring.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جوکھم}}
\textbf{\ur{جوکھم}} — \emph{jokham} — \textquotedblleft{}a risk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پہاڑ} \ur{پر} \ur{چڑھنا} \ur{جوکھم} \ur{کا} \ur{کام} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pahāṛ par chaṛhnā jokham kā kām hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Climbing a mountain is risky work.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جوکھم}} (\emph{jokham}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jokham}, \textquotedblleft{}risk, danger\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{yōgakṣēmá}, \textquotedblleft{}the keeping of one's property\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10527): the sense probably moved through the charge paid against loss to the risk itself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jokham}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jokham}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pahāṛ par chaṛhnā jokham kā kām hai.} — Climbing a mountain is risky work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for bold, then the Urdu for daring, then say \emph{jokham} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جوکھم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A risk\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لڑنا} (laṛnā)}{لڑنا (laṛnā)}]{\ur{لڑنا} (laṛnā) — to fight; to stand up (to)}

\label{lesson:UR-C460-larna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for daring, then the Urdu for a risk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{لڑنا}} — \emph{laṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fight; to stand up (to)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{اپنے} \ur{حق} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{لڑا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh apne haq ke liye laṛā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He fought for his rights.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بیماری} \ur{سے} \ur{لڑی}, \emph{voh bīmārī se laṛī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لڑنا}} (\emph{laṛnā}) is inherited from \emph{laḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}fight\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 10920).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
